newsitem.title: ROMANIA: THREE FOREIGN COMPANIES BID FOR ROMANIAN REFINERY.
newsitem.headline: THREE FOREIGN COMPANIES BID FOR ROMANIAN REFINERY.

text.p: Romania's main privatisation agency, the State Ownership Fund (FPS), said on Friday it would start talks with three foreign companies next week to sell 51 percent of the Petromidia oil refinery.

Stefan Brad, a member of the FPS board, told journalists talks would start on Tuesday with Daewoo of South Korea and soon after with Glencore of Switzerland and Petromidia USA Ltd. All three bidders, he said, had lodged bank guarantees.
The FPS rejected two local bidders, Atheneum Oil and Concept, due to their failure to submit guarantees. The Fund's representatives issued no data about Petromidia or the bidders.

Petromidia is one of Romania's most modern refineries, on the Black Sea coast. It was originally on a list for restructuring presented by the government earlier this year, but is now being offered for sell-off.
Petromidia was modernised after the 1989 fall of communism at a cost of about $50 million.
